title: Every bid recommendation on /draft ignores the user's remaining budget — with $4 left the board says "Win at $69 / Max bid $80 / Push up to $48"
claimUnderTest: draft-logic.js's header documents Winning bid(p) = min(Theoretical Max, topCompetitorMax + 1) and describes effectiveBudgetFor as 'the maximum $ a team can actually bid on a single player right now'. The /draft modal advertises an overpay guard.
observed: theoreticalMaxBid, myMaxBid, myWinningBid and enforceUpTo are computed from preDraft x aggression x tierInflation x phaseMultiplier and capped ONLY by topCompetitorMax + 1. Not one of them reads myRemaining or effectiveBudgetByIdx[myTeamIdx]. effectiveBudgetFor() is applied to RIVALS only (line 480-485 skips myTeamIdx). bidStatus() classifies against myWinningBid, so a bid 6x the user's cash reads 'Push up'. The only modal warning fires on amt > myWinningBid, never on amt > myRemaining, so entering an unaffordable amount below the ceiling shows nothing at all.

reproduction.expected: a bid ceiling <= myRemaining ($4), or an affordability warning
reproduction.actual: myRemaining=4, Sonny Styles myMaxBid=$80, myWinningBid=$69, enforceUpTo=$48, bidStatus($24) = {level:'push', label:'Push up'}

numericProof.formula: theoreticalMaxBid = floor(preDraft * (1 + aggression*(BA-1)) * inflation*tierMult * phaseMultiplier); myWinningBid = min(theoreticalMaxBid, topCompetitorMax + 1); NO min(..., myRemaining) term exists

userImpact: Mid-draft the user reads 'Win at $69' on a player they can only pay $4 for, bids, and either loses the auction after driving the price up or wins a bid they cannot fund. The bid-status chip actively says 'Push up' on an amount 6x their cash.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced at runtime with concrete numbers and the bidStatus consequence, which the prior finding did not quantify. The slot half of the prior finding is split out as W10-F002.

whatWorks: The rival-side ceiling (effectiveBudgetFor over other teams) is applied correctly and topCompetitorMax does cap the recommendation from above; the overpay banner fires correctly for the case it does cover (amount above the rival ceiling).
rootCause: myWinningBid was designed as 'the price that beats the field', and no second clamp for 'the price I can actually pay' was ever added. effectiveBudgetFor exists and would answer it, but is deliberately skipped for myTeamIdx.
requiredRepair: Clamp every emitted bid number by effectiveBudgetFor(myRemaining, mySlotsRemaining) and add an affordability state to bidStatus distinct from 'pass'. Add an amt > myRemaining branch to the modal warning.
dependencies: Depends on W10-F002 — mySlotsRemaining is currently wrong, so the clamp must not be built on the capped slot count.
